title: Encoding, Normalization & Parser Differentials
description: Different interpretations of the same input across browsers, proxies, and servers.

attacks.name: Double URL encoding
attacks.desc: Encoding a path twice can bypass a filter that decodes only once while a later layer decodes again.
attacks.prevention: Decode and normalize once at a defined boundary, then validate the canonical value used by routing and file access.

attacks.name: Overlong UTF-8
attacks.desc: Invalid or overlong UTF-8 may be interpreted differently by validation and routing components.
attacks.prevention: Reject invalid UTF-8 rather than allowing different components to repair or decode it differently.

attacks.name: Unicode normalization
attacks.desc: Unicode normalization can make distinct-looking strings compare equal after validation has already occurred.
attacks.prevention: Normalize identifiers consistently before validation and comparison, including Unicode normalization rules.

attacks.name: Homoglyph bypass
attacks.desc: Lookalike characters can evade literal string checks while appearing identical to a reader.
attacks.prevention: Use normalized machine identifiers for authorization and warn users about deceptive lookalike display names.

attacks.name: Path confusion
attacks.desc: Different path parsers may disagree about separators, semicolons, nulls, dots, or duplicate slashes.
attacks.prevention: Resolve canonical paths before policy checks and reject alternate path forms that change the backend target.

attacks.name: Matrix parameters
attacks.desc: Semicolon-delimited matrix parameters can change route matching when intermediaries and frameworks parse them differently.

attacks.name: Case sensitivity bypass
attacks.desc: Case differences in a path may bypass a case-sensitive check when another layer treats paths case-insensitively.

attacks.name: Content-Type confusion
attacks.desc: A declared Content-Type that does not match the body can trigger different parsers or validation rules.

attacks.name: X-HTTP-Method-Override
attacks.desc: A method-override header can turn an allowed POST into a different backend action if authorization is inconsistent.

attacks.name: MIME sniffing
attacks.desc: Without a no-sniff policy, browsers may interpret a response as executable content despite its declared MIME type.

attacks.name: Multipart boundary abuse
attacks.desc: Malformed multipart boundaries can cause upload validators and application parsers to extract different content.

attacks.name: JSON parser differential
attacks.desc: Duplicate JSON keys and unusual values can produce different objects in different parsers.

attacks.name: Null byte injection
attacks.desc: A null byte can truncate a value in one component while another component retains the full string.

attacks.name: Type juggling
attacks.desc: Loose type comparison can treat distinct values as equal and bypass checks that expect exact matches.

attacks.name: Wildcard/glob abuse
attacks.desc: Wildcard characters in filters can broaden a lookup or match more records than the caller intended.
